The conduit metaphor is a pervasive, but often invisible, way of looking at language.
the "conduit" metaphor is the most frequently used and that it is a frame conflict metaphor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of communication as an activity.
the study of the messages, and the messages themselves, and the study of the communications facilities which belong not to society, or to any other large group of people, but to individuals.
the study of the "messages and communications facilities which constitute the human condition."
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Schon's chapter is a very important contribution, but that it is incomplete without the addition of a study of the role of communication in the process of problem setting.
the "frame conflicts" that are so important for social science, and for social life itself, are in large part a result of a lack of communication between people, and between disciplines.
the "stories people tell about troublesome social situations" are the very messages that constitute the social situations themselves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have not yet begun to understand the messages that we send and receive.
we have been trying to understand how people think and act in terms of their messages and communications facilities.

the "stories that we tell about troublesome situations," and the "frame conflicts that we have in our language about our language," are precisely the messages and communications which constitute the "society" that Schon wants to understand.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are not the only ones that can help people.

we are all storytellers, and we all have stories we are trying to tell about ourselves and our lives, and we all need to be heard, and we all want to be heard, but we are often not heard, because the stories we are trying, to tell are not the stories that are being told, and the stories we are telling are not the stories we are being asked to tell.
, if we want to understand how people make meaning and communicate, we need to understand the role of language and communication in the process.
